newsitem.title: UK: London gold fixes touch higher in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: London gold fixes touch higher in thin trade.

text.p: Light buying lifted gold prices about 40 cents from opening levels ahead of the Thursday morning fixing in an otherwise very quiet market, dealers said.
"Activity is slowing down and business has been very quiet. We have not seen any real new trend in gold so far," according to an analyst based in continental Europe.
Gold was fixed at $369.60 per ounce compared with $368.70 on Wednesday afternoon and a close then of $368.85/$369.35.
Dealers said there was no clear trend in the price overnight as the market steadily slowed down ahead of the Christmas holiday next week.
To establish a direction gold would have to get into the $372-$373 range and that would mean taking out resistance at $370 on the way.
"I can see gold trying to get over at least $370 today," the analyst said.
However, dealers in London pointed out that the market's lack of liquidity could mean a relatively volatile session, albeit in a fairly tight range.
"No new business is expected before Christmas. The producers and funds have done what they had to do and industrial interest will not be back before January," one market professional said.
The OTC option expiry on Friday was likely to feature the $370 strike price, given that the market had been hovering below that level since December 9.
"I'd be surprised if the option expiry had much of an impact at this stage in the year," a dealer said.
Silver picked up on fund buying in New York on Wednesday afternoon but was virtually static on Thursday in London, adding only a cent to its unchanged opening of $4.85/$4.87.
"It's been ignored so far. It didn't even move behind gold," a dealer said.
A move into the $4.90s would mean the price attracting selling from the pile of physical silver hanging over the market.
"Heavy selling could be expected approaching $5.00 but support was available at $4.70," an analyst said.
Platinum was indicated at $371.00/$372.00, up 50 cents.
"Almost all of platinum's gains have been from short-covering. There hasn't been any new buying," he said.
Palladium was very quiet and 50 cents lower at $117.75/$118.75.
